passage: In the reception hall's office, the manager laid out the floor plan, the menu list and the deposit form. Kavitha's father asked, "Is this all right with you two?" Kavitha and Jeevan glanced at each other. "Do whatever you think, Uncle," Jeevan said. Kavitha nodded, to avoid any argument. Three weeks later they arrived for the tasting. The hall was vast and echoing, and the menu was almost all sweets and rich gravies. They had wanted a small garden lunch. The deposit was not refundable. "We can adjust the menu a little," the manager said kindly, "but the hall is fixed." Kavitha swallowed and looked at Jeevan. Neither spoke.

qa.q: What did Jeevan say when asked if the plan was all right?
qa.a: Jeevan said, "Do whatever you think, Uncle."

qa.q: Why did Kavitha nod when Jeevan said that?
qa.a: Kavitha wanted to avoid an argument, and now feels dismayed and stuck at the tasting.

qa.q: What could Kavitha and Jeevan have done at the office, and why?
qa.a: They could have said what they wanted, such as a small garden lunch, and asked to see options, because choices are easy to change before a deposit is paid.

qa.q: How might Kavitha's father have felt on hearing the couple was unhappy?
qa.a: Kavitha's father would probably feel surprised and sorry, having believed the couple was content when they said to do whatever the father thought.

grounding: Illustrates a couple avoiding conflict by telling the parents to do whatever they think, then finding the venue and menu do not fit and change is costly.

passage:
Dear Hemant,

You asked how the wedding plans are going. Honestly? Badly, and it's my own fault.
When Mummy and Papa asked what kind of venue we wanted, Jaishree and I said, "Whatever you think is best." We both hate arguments, and we thought it would keep the peace.
Last weekend they showed us what they'd booked: a banquet hall on the highway, three hundred covers, and a buffet that is mostly non-vegetarian. Jaishree's family is strictly vegetarian. We had always pictured something small near her home town.
We called the hall. The advance is non-refundable, and the menu has already been sent to the caterer. Changing now means losing the advance and upsetting Papa, who arranged it all himself.
I keep thinking about how easy it would have been to say one sentence back in March.
Anyway. Tell me about your new job. I need some good news.

Pranav

qa.q: What kind of food is mostly on the buffet?
qa.a: A buffet that is mostly non-vegetarian.

qa.q: How does Pranav feel about the wedding plans?
qa.a: Pranav feels regretful and frustrated, wishing they had spoken up back in March.

qa.q: What could Pranav and Jaishree have said in March instead of "Whatever you think is best"?
qa.a: They could have shared a few clear wishes, like a small vegetarian event near Jaishree's home town, and left the rest to the parents.

qa.q: How might Pranav's Papa feel if the couple now tries to change the booking?
qa.a: Papa might feel hurt and confused, since he arranged everything himself believing the couple had no preferences.

grounding: It shows a couple avoiding conflict by leaving decisions to the parents and later finding the venue and menu don't fit their wishes when changing means losses.

passage:
So, Leela, you asked why I looked miserable in the photos. I'll tell you, since you're getting married next year.
When Karan and I got engaged, both sets of parents were so excited. Every time they asked, "What do you want for the reception?" I said, "Whatever you think." I didn't want to fight. Karan said the same.
I, Vandana, the person who plans everything at work, just stepped back.
Three months later, they showed us the venue: a huge hotel ballroom, gold everywhere, a menu of dishes neither of us eats. I'd always wanted the reception outdoors, with simple food and a few friends.
By then the hotel advance was paid and the invitations were printed. Cancelling meant losing money and hurting our parents. So we smiled through it.
Please, Leela, tell them the three things you care about early. That's all it takes.

qa.q: What kind of venue did the parents book for the reception?
qa.a: A huge hotel ballroom, gold everywhere.

qa.q: How did Vandana feel at the reception, and why?
qa.a: Vandana felt miserable and trapped, because the venue and menu didn't fit what Vandana wanted and it was too late to change without losses.

qa.q: What was Vandana's key choice in the story, and what could Vandana have done instead?
qa.a: The key choice was saying "Whatever you think" every time; Vandana could have shared a few clear wishes early, like an outdoor reception with simple food.

qa.q: How might the parents have felt if they had learned the couple was unhappy?
qa.a: They would likely feel hurt and confused, having planned with love while believing the couple had no preferences.

grounding: It shows someone avoiding conflict by leaving the plans to the parents, then finding the venue and menu don't fit their wishes when changing would mean losses.
